A second investigator, starting fresh with the same tools, tested the kind of each fault in your draft answer. Their findings:

### `product-catalog`: you said `pod_unavailable`. They conclude `network_partition` (confidence: low).
Scope: Affected: the calls from frontend (GetProduct), checkout (GetProduct) and recommendation (ListProducts) into product-catalog, which all fail within 0.1 to 0.7 ms with Error status, and the product-catalog database calls, which fell from 60 a minute to 0.2 because no requests reach the service. Not affected: the product-catalog pod itself, which keeps reporting container and pod metrics under the same name to the end of the window (sparser, about half the normal rate), and the other calls from frontend and checkout (cart, ad, shipping and so on), which stay normal. The fault sits on the connection into product-catalog, not inside the service.
Ruled out:
- `pod_unavailable`: The claimed kind is not supported. The pod is the same name in both periods (product-catalog-798f5d7bdb-j4tjg) with no restart and no uptime reset, and it keeps emitting its full container and pod metric set (CPU, memory, filesystem) from 05:22:17 to 05:26:42, the end of the window. A pod that stayed gone would have its metrics fall away. Its spans and logs stop, but that is explained by no requests arriving, so they do not separate a dead pod from a cut link.
- `pod_failure`: No new pod name, no restart and no uptime reset for product-catalog in the incident window, so there is no kill-and-restart signature.
- `network_delay`: The calls to product-catalog are not slow; they fail at once (0.11 ms, 0.36 ms, 0.65 ms average). Delay would show slow successful calls with the 25th, 50th and 95th percentiles rising together.
- `application_method_slow`: The product-catalog Server span for GetProduct is absent (one span only, at 05:21:59.7), so there is no self-reported slow method time to measure. The callers' spans are the failing ones, and they fail before reaching the service.
- `database_call_slow`: Product-catalog's sql.conn.query client calls dropped from 60 a minute to 0.2, which reflects no traffic arriving rather than slow statements.
- `http_aborted`: Not confirmed and not fully excluded. The failures are fast, which fits an aborted exchange, but the error text (for example Unexpected end of file or connection reset) is not in the schema I could query, and the failures cover all product-catalog gRPC calls from three callers rather than one route. The fast failure matches a refused connection better.
- `dns_lookup_failed`: No name-resolution error text was found in the telemetry I could query, and the callers' Error spans were not checked for UnknownHost text because the status message field is not in the schema. Not tested directly.
Evidence:
- Product-catalog has one pod name, product-catalog-798f5d7bdb-j4tjg, with 11 RSS samples from 05:22:17 to 05:26:42 and no uptime or restart rows. Its only logs are 6 INFO lines between 05:21:59.74 and 05:21:59.85, and its only spans are one sql.conn.query client span and one GetProduct server span at 05:21:59.7.

kind_checks.scope: Affected: the calls from frontend (GetProduct), checkout (GetProduct) and recommendation (ListProducts) into product-catalog, which all fail within 0.1 to 0.7 ms with Error status, and the product-catalog database calls, which fell from 60 a minute to 0.2 because no requests reach the service. Not affected: the product-catalog pod itself, which keeps reporting container and pod metrics under the same name to the end of the window (sparser, about half the normal rate), and the other calls from frontend and checkout (cart, ad, shipping and so on), which stay normal. The fault sits on the connection into product-catalog, not inside the service.

ruled_out.why: The claimed kind is not supported. The pod is the same name in both periods (product-catalog-798f5d7bdb-j4tjg) with no restart and no uptime reset, and it keeps emitting its full container and pod metric set (CPU, memory, filesystem) from 05:22:17 to 05:26:42, the end of the window. A pod that stayed gone would have its metrics fall away. Its spans and logs stop, but that is explained by no requests arriving, so they do not separate a dead pod from a cut link.
No new pod name, no restart and no uptime reset for product-catalog in the incident window, so there is no kill-and-restart signature.
The calls to product-catalog are not slow; they fail at once (0.11 ms, 0.36 ms, 0.65 ms average). Delay would show slow successful calls with the 25th, 50th and 95th percentiles rising together.

The product-catalog Server span for GetProduct is absent (one span only, at 05:21:59.7), so there is no self-reported slow method time to measure. The callers' spans are the failing ones, and they fail before reaching the service.
Product-catalog's sql.conn.query client calls dropped from 60 a minute to 0.2, which reflects no traffic arriving rather than slow statements.

Not confirmed and not fully excluded. The failures are fast, which fits an aborted exchange, but the error text (for example Unexpected end of file or connection reset) is not in the schema I could query, and the failures cover all product-catalog gRPC calls from three callers rather than one route. The fast failure matches a refused connection better.

No name-resolution error text was found in the telemetry I could query, and the callers' Error spans were not checked for UnknownHost text because the status message field is not in the schema. Not tested directly.

**Verdict: `pod_unavailable` is not supported. The evidence fits a cut connection to a live product-catalog pod, which is the network-blocking class (`network_partition` or `network_loss`, scored as one answer). Confidence is moderate-low.**

**Evidence against `pod_unavailable`**

- **Same pod, no restart.** The only product-catalog pod in both periods is `product-catalog-798f5d7bdb-j4tjg`. There is no new pod name, no uptime reset and no restart count change. A pod kill-and-restart would show one of these.
- **The pod kept reporting to the end of the window.** In the incident window, the full container and pod metric set (CPU, memory, filesystem, node utilisation) has 11 samples each, from 05:22:17 to 05:26:42. Normal has 24 RSS samples over about 4.7 minutes, roughly 5 a minute. Incident has 11 over about 4.4 minutes, roughly 2.5 a minute. The rate halved; it did not fall away. `pod_unavailable` should leave a gap that runs to the end of the window.
- **The silence in spans and logs has a simpler explanation.** Product-catalog's own spans and logs stop when its traffic stops. Its `sql.conn.query` calls fell from 60/min to 0.2/min, which is what happens when no requests arrive. A live pod with a cut link looks the same on spans and logs as a dead one, so the spans and logs do not separate the two.

**Evidence for a cut connection (`network_partition` class)**

- **Calls fail at once with the peer alive.** Callers' Error spans take about 0.1 ms (checkout GetProduct, 19 calls), 0.36 ms (frontend GetProduct, 136 calls) and 0.65 ms (recommendation ListProducts, 29 calls). The guidance says a client that cannot connect gives up in well under a millisecond. Frontend-proxy returns 500 with a 21-byte body in about 2 ms on product routes.
- **Nothing is slow or timed out.** Failures are fast, not timeouts, which fits a partition and does not fit a hung peer.
- **Everything else in the caller path looks normal.** Frontend's error share rises, but its other calls and its own logs are unchanged, so the damage is confined to the calls into product-catalog.

**Limits**

- The `status_message` and error text of the Error spans are not in the schema, so I could not read the connection-refused or unavailable text. That text would sharpen the call.
- The case has no `hubble_*` per-connection metrics, so the link itself cannot be observed directly.
- The RSS collapse to 0.35 MB, which the lead cited, rests on 11 samples. It is not a reliable sign of a dead process, and I did not use it.
- The network-blocking class covers loss and partition; this data does not separate them, and I did not try to.
